title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report, outlining its plan to establish and promote public standards for artificial intelligence. It commits to working with industry, academia and regulators to develop clear, transparent guidelines that ensure AI systems are safe, reliable and trustworthy.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The EU Regulation 2024/1689 sets uniform rules for using artificial intelligence throughout Europe and updates other related laws. Its purpose is to make AI safer, more transparent, and easier to develop, while protecting people and ensuring consistent standards across member states.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has issued a policy detailing how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to protect exam integrity, fairness, and transparency. The policy, released in response to requests from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, sets out guidelines, risk assessments, and monitoring procedures to ensure AI tools enhance rather than undermine the quality and reliability of qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted materials are used in training and developing AI systems, and it evaluates the legal, economic, and ethical impacts of these practices. It provides recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the need for innovation in artificial intelligence.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its strategy for tackling the rapid growth of artificial intelligence. The response highlights key priorities such as strengthening regulation, boosting research and development, ensuring ethical use, and fostering collaboration between industry, academia, and government.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference and FAQs for a committee that will review artificial intelligence and public standards. It explains the committee’s purpose, scope, and key questions they will address in their assessment.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its perspectives on AI regulation. The submission addresses key concerns about how AI should be governed and regulated to ensure responsible development and use.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how AI will change the way medical products are regulated, focusing on safety, effectiveness, and transparency. It applies the guidelines from the AI White Paper to ensure new technologies meet high standards before reaching patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence body for its size. It focuses on using AI to improve operations, decision‑making, and strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to tap into AI’s opportunities while keeping its risks in check. It details strategies for using AI safely and responsibly to improve transport services and infrastructure.
